examples.label: Screenshot every host from the nmap XML into a report

notes: Screenshots let you triage dozens of apps in one pass; it also grabs server headers and default-page fingerprints. Point it at the nmap XML, not a flat URL list, so ports are preserved.
name: EyeWitness - Screenshot Web Applications
description: Takes screenshots of every web app from an Nmap XML, letting you triage many hosts visually and spot default/login/admin pages fast.

defense.why_it_works: EyeWitness uses a headless browser to screenshot web services discovered from Nmap XML or URL lists, categorising results by technology detected for rapid triage of large environments.
defense.prerequisites: List of targets from a prior Nmap scan or URL list. Network access to HTTP/HTTPS ports.
defense.impact: Attacker rapidly identifies default-credential panels, exposed management UIs (Jenkins, PRTG, Tomcat Manager), and outdated login pages across a network segment.
defense.detection: Headless browser requests generate characteristic HTTP headers. Sequential requests from one IP with short delay. IDS signature for EyeWitness User-Agent.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (sequential requests, minimal interaction) | IDS/WAF alerts for scanning UA strings
defense.prevention: Require VPN/network-level auth before management interfaces are reachable. Suppress version banners. Block known scanning tool User-Agents at WAF.
defense.evasion: Throttle and randomize the screenshot/probe sweep; use a normal User-Agent; scope to in-scope hosts to avoid a fan-out pattern.
